# Versioned compatibility evidence

The current public evidence matrix contains 3,921 total rows: 3,208 decode /
inspect / verify rows and 713 encode rows. Of those, 3,208 decode rows are
active and 686 encode rows are active; 27 encode rows remain planned.

## WebP lossless EXIF metadata without prefix — 2026-11-10

For `image-slash-star#9h5w`, added active parity case
`encode:webp:enc_lossless_exif_unprefixed_metadata_reuse`. It gives the
lossless WebP metadata-reuse path a valid EXIF TIFF payload without the optional
`Exif\0\0` prefix, covering the fallback arm in
`attach_metadata_reusing_output`. Pinned Pillow 12.2.0 and the Rust encoder
produce the same 74-byte output; re-decoding preserves exact 1×1 RGB pixels.

The selected parity run passed 1/1, with four public encode calls and zero
panics. Coverage MCP's retained full-parity report had identified the
unprefixed-payload arm at `src/codecs/webp/encode/mod.rs:949` as uncovered. The
selected report no longer lists that arm as missing; other branches in the
metadata-reuse function remain uncovered. Coverage MCP marks this local report
source identity unverified and test attribution unknown, so this confirms the
focused branch hit rather than an aggregate coverage change. The report's
SHA-256 is
`bd252dfeefda56fadbdab053add8710b4cdc7a6dae7767ad5481307f1a6a37e1`; its local
receipt SHA-256 is
`3bb9f9d92f22c97164cb16453102ae99cd7af0af5cb61b1c1bf0dc001aaddc38`.
Mode case indexes remain at 40 decode entries and 59 encode entries.

Report:
`.coverage-mcp/local-evidence/selected/20261110-webp-exif-unprefixed/coverage.json`.

## WebP scalar-mode encoder parity — 2026-11-09

Added five Pillow 12.2.0 parity rows for WebP encoding from TIFF `I;16B`, `I`,
and `F` sources. They cover big-endian source metadata, signed 32-bit clamp
boundaries, float conversion, and the token-aware preparation checkpoint on a
128×128 float image. WebP converts the scalar transfer samples to grayscale RGB
using the same native-order sample interpretation and saturating conversion as
Pillow. The public-mode error contract now keeps `I` and `F` in the accepted mode
set and continues checking structured errors for unsupported modes. The
append-only mode encode index now includes `I;16B` → `Rgb8`, `I` → `Rgb8`, and
`F` → `Rgb8`.

The focused selected parity run passed 5/5 rows with exact encoded bytes and
pixel output. `make lint` and `make lint-x86-simd` pass, including the strict
x86-64 SSE2 baseline and AVX2 Clippy builds. No unit tests were added. The
selected LLVM report measures 6,752/142,788 lines (4.7287%), 1,130/32,114
branches (3.5187%), 455/9,180 functions (4.9564%), and 9,578/221,186 regions
(4.3303%) for this run. Coverage MCP was not queried; its local receipt marks
source identity unverified and test attribution unknown, so these selected
counts are not a repository-wide coverage claim.

Report:
`.coverage-mcp/local-evidence/selected/20261109T061152.051311Z-3c05f788dd644b3eb82e8a57779bd4e0/coverage.json`

## TIFF palette-extra mode identity — 2026-11-09

Added `decode:tiff:palette_alpha_separate_planar`: Pillow inspects and verifies
the separate-plane header as `PA`, then rejects pixel decoding. The new
`decode:tiff:palette_unspecified_extra_sample` row covers a contiguous indexed
image with `ExtraSamples=0`; Pillow retains `P` identity and drops the second
sample. TIFF inspection now preserves these header identities independently of
pixel storage, while decoding keeps Pillow's malformed result for separate
PA planes. The existing PA encoder parity row verifies encoded header and
decoded transfer identity through the append-only sink.

The focused selection passed 5/5: `decode:tiff:compression_none`,
`decode:tiff:palette_alpha`, `decode:tiff:palette_alpha_separate_planar`,
`decode:tiff:palette_unspecified_extra_sample`, and
`encode:tiff:enc_palette_alpha`. Coverage MCP reports no missing branch groups
at `inspect.rs:439` or the `decode_ifd` guard at `decode.rs:253`. Matrix
validation checked the append-only mode decode/encode case indexes, and the
encoder row exercised the append-only sink. Its selected LLVM report records
2,551/142,734 lines (1.7872%), 266/32,112 branches (0.8284%), 244/9,174
functions (2.6597%), and 3,540/221,113 regions (1.6010%) across the
instrumented crate. Coverage MCP labels this local report source identity
unverified and test attribution unknown; these selected-case totals are not a
repository-wide coverage claim.

Report:
`.coverage-mcp/local-evidence/selected/20261109T035617.440441Z-48d4a4b2422f41cb8869af6fda5c812f/coverage.json`
(SHA-256 `a5012a8c32501582f9438a5dd87aa65493ae6b07b962697637643c901ab66ecba`).

## Big-endian 16-bit TIFF encoder identity — 2026-11-09

Added two Pillow parity rows for a source decoded as `I;16B`. Uncompressed
TIFF output now retains the big-endian `MM` header and `I;16B` raster identity;
Deflate with horizontal prediction matches Pillow's little-endian `II` output
and normalized `I;16` identity. The encoder converts carrier samples only for
the raw big-endian path and includes Pillow's single-sample tag on compressed
16-bit grayscale output. A new manifest-driven parity row covers a two-page
`I;16` TIFF sequence whose second frame is converted to `I;16B`; Pillow and
Rust both reject that mixed-byte-order save.

The new focused parity selection passed 1/1:
`encode:tiff:enc_error_mixed_sample_byte_order_sequence`. The earlier TIFF
selection at commit `431c3e6` passed 66 encode rows, one big-endian decode row,
and the now-retired target-only sequence contract (68/68 total). The combined
selection was not rerun after replacing that contract with the Pillow parity
row. No unit tests were added.

## AVIF monochrome padded-edge context parity — 2026-11-07

The 2026-11-06 sweep passed 244 active grayscale and monochrome AVIF decode
parity rows but did not execute the right-starting arm at

`decode:avif:lossless_monochrome_padded_right_context_1x128` uses a pinned
1x128 all-lossless monochrome image. Its 4x4 coded leaves extend into AV1's
padded right edge, so the complete streamed-lossless path declines the
one-pixel width and the monochrome fallback must decode those leaves to build

## AVIF B16x8 16×7 reachability probe — 2026-11-06

A 16×7 8-bit I420 sequence was produced from a fixture-only copy of libaom
configured to force a horizontal split. Pillow 12.2, dav1d 1.5.3, and AOM
3.13.2 decoded the sequence. The temporary selected-matrix run checked exact
pixels for frame 0 and sequence decoding and structure; it did not assert
exact pixels for frame 1. A temporary coverage-instrumented build did not call
`exact_inter_block_geometry`, and the selected Coverage MCP query still
reported the false `visible_height == 8` outcome at
`src/codecs/avif/av1/block.rs:49555` as missing.

This probe does not qualify as a parity fixture for that branch. It also does
not prove the branch unreachable for all valid AV1 inputs. These reports are
exploratory; Coverage MCP marks source identity `unverified` and test
attribution `unknown`. The probe did not add a permanent fixture or matrix
row. Reports:
`.coverage-mcp/local-evidence/selected/20261106-b16x8-forced-height7-probe/coverage.json`
(SHA-256
`626110884caa6935ecf564969c0b5c85737069e63f4d67824b9f6a6e71bb9bd9`; receipt
SHA-256
`91acdbdd95198bf27c6cac7fc9c58c1e48e16f435aa3d52b8d1539950e4ad4ab`) and
`.coverage-mcp/local-evidence/selected/20261106-b16x8-forced-height7-instrumented-probe/coverage.json`
(SHA-256
`c73712e56050bbf8dcd1461dece49d9fe717c261eec5b86647f3fedcc8465b9c`; receipt
SHA-256
`eb631124713e46455e827b3b2c16c87c06114d9b9592ab114ac9cfe47a943ef9`).

The current source path explains why this input did not reach the predicate.
`decode_inter_transform_size` admits a lossy `B16x8` split plan only for a full
16×8 visible extent. Its lossless-grid admission allows clipped extents only
for the separately bounded B32 profile. `validate_inter_transform_plan_geometry`
calls `exact_inter_block_geometry` only for non-single plans. Thus the current
admitted plan paths cannot call the B16x8 predicate with width 16 and a clipped
height. This is a source-path finding for the current implementation, not a
claim that every valid AV1 stream has this restriction. No public parity case
has yet shown a supported way to reach the false height comparison; revisit it
if the admitted B16x8 plan grammar changes.

## AVIF bounded C-string parser consolidation — 2026-11-06

The container and sample readers each had a missing-terminator path that
reported `NeedMore` when their bounded payload lacked a NUL byte. Both readers
are reached only after the enclosing box or sample extent has been validated;
an incomplete outer box is rejected by the whole-input parser first. The
incremental branches were therefore unreachable through the public API. A
shared `c_string_len` helper now returns the existing malformed-input contract
for an unterminated bounded payload and keeps the common search inline in
production builds. No fixture or private unit test was added.

is `unverified` and test attribution is `unknown`.

## AV1 partition walker even-grid invariant — 2026-11-04

The AV1 partition walker derives frame extents as twice the number of 8-pixel
blocks, so frame bounds are even in its four-pixel grid. Tile origins and
superblock roots are aligned to at least 16 grid units, and recursive offsets
before level 4 are even. A level-4 node inside its root therefore has at least
two grid units remaining and cannot enter the old no-split boundary-leaf path.
That path and its redundant frame-bound checks were removed; valid partition
and block parsing is unchanged, with fewer checks in the recursive walk.

Four existing Pillow-backed AVIF parity rows passed: 10-bit I420 CDEF at
15x16, a 73x64 lossless monochrome grid, 10-bit lossless I444, and lossless
I444 film grain. The selected report is
`.coverage-mcp/local-evidence/selected/av1-partition-even-grid-20261104/coverage.json`
(SHA-256 `561e37ac…2f81d6`). Its local execution receipt records 4/4 passed
and no source changes during the run; Coverage MCP identity and test
attribution remain unverified. `make lint` passed formatting and all configured
strict Clippy lanes, including coverage and AVIF-only builds. No parity rows or
unit tests were added.

An ARM64 A-B-B-A release probe of the 2048x128 AVIF sequence used two runs of
42 and 120 timed decodes per revision. Their directions differed (+3.4% and
-2.2%); pooled medians were 9.887 ms before and 9.857 ms after. This is no
measurable speed change, not a speedup claim. Raw samples and host/build details
are retained under
`.coverage-mcp/local-evidence/perf/av1-partition-even-grid-20261104/`.
The measurement is ARM64-only and says nothing about SSE2 or AVX2 runtime
performance.

## AV1 CDEF aligned chroma edge parity — 2026-11-03

Added `decode:avif:coverage_i420_intra_cdef_10bit_15x16` to cover a CDEF
boundary not reached by the existing odd-size cases. With a 15-pixel I420
luma width, the corresponding visible chroma width is 8 and ends on a complete
four-sample CDEF block. This reaches the in-plane boundary path for chroma
while the luma plane still exercises its partial right edge.

The case exposed an incorrect edge extension in `frame_coordinate`: samples
beyond a coded plane were clamped to its last coded sample. AV1 treats those
tap locations as unavailable. The decoder now rejects coordinates at or past
the coded extent and still preserves hidden samples that lie inside it. The
new row initially differed from the pinned Pillow output in 30 of 720 RGB
bytes at the final column; after the fix, the exact output matches. The
existing 9x9 and 9x16 CDEF rows plus this 15x16 case pass 3/3.

The final one-row selection passes 1/1 and records 798 in-plane and 819
out-of-plane decisions at the coded-extent guard. Its selected LLVM report is

## AVIF fixed-four CDF shared-shift trial — 2026-11-02

The fixed-four adaptive-symbol reader accounts for 1,240 of 4,602 leaf samples
in the retained lossy compound profile. Its three CDF adaptation branches
motivated a bounded shared-shift experiment. Writing a probability as
`p = q * 2^r + t`, the upward adjustment is exactly
`2^(15-r) - q - [t != 0]` for AV1 rates 5 through 7. The candidate shares
`p >> r` between both directions, with an explicit remainder correction;
symbol selection, normalization, count updates and failure handling stay intact.
It adds no unsafe Rust, dependency, public API or runtime hook.

Native ARM64 assembly replaces all three adaptation branches with conditional
selections. Each matching routine has 133 instructions instead of 135, while
the 96-byte stack frame and refill path stay the same. This does not establish
a performance gain: more of the arithmetic executes on common downward updates.
Both source-bound binaries match live pinned Pillow pixels and shapes on all
13 complete still/sequence workloads before timing, including translated motion
and split/disjoint extent controls.

One predeclared independent cohort retains 156 process samples: three A-B-B-A
cycles over 13 workloads, ten warmup calls and a three-second sample target,
with 30 to 500,000 iterations. Complete public decode and result destruction
are timed after reading the input. No Cargo build or test campaign overlaps
the measurements. The shared Apple M3 Pro ARM64 host runs macOS 15.7.7 and
Rust 1.96.1. This cohort is not pooled with earlier experiments.

| Workload | Overall median latency change | Changes in the three cycles |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Lossy compound sequence | -1.104% | -1.127%, -1.630%, -0.640% |
| Lossless compound sequence | +1.879% | +1.443%, +2.215%, +0.819% |
| Ordinary 10-bit monochrome super-resolution control | -4.254% | -4.079%, -3.672%, -3.801% |

The admission rule requires at least a 3% overall gain and a 3% gain in at least
two cycles on either profiled compound workload, with no control repeatedly
more than 3% slower overall. Neither profiled workload qualifies. The ordinary

## JPEG Adobe marker precedence and color defaults — 2026-11-01

JPEG color interpretation now follows the last valid Adobe APP14 marker before
the first scan. Later markers remain retained metadata and cannot change the
header's color choice. Previously the parser kept the first recognized marker,
and a first marker after the scans could incorrectly reinterpret unmarked CMYK.
Four-component JPEGs also follow libjpeg's YCCK default for unsupported nonzero
Adobe transforms. The parser normalizes those values once when it captures the
header interpretation; the raw APP14 payloads remain intact. Baseline and
progressive reconstruction source files are identical to the preceding batch.
The [pinned marker reader](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libjpeg-turbo/libjpeg-turbo/3.1.4.1/src/jdmarker.c)
and [header color defaults](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libjpeg-turbo/libjpeg-turbo/3.1.4.1/src/jdapimin.c)
are retained with source hashes alongside the live Pillow observations.

## RGB JPEG color semantics and progressive row assembly — 2026-11-01

Raw RGB JPEG components now bypass YCbCr conversion in baseline and
progressive decoding. The parser captures three-component color interpretation
at the first SOS marker: JFIF implies YCbCr, Adobe transform zero selects RGB,
and unmarked `R/G/B` component identifiers select RGB. The new cases check
JFIF precedence, an explicit Adobe YCbCr override, missing Adobe metadata, and
a conflicting Adobe marker after the scan, which cannot change the header-time
color choice. Previously, those RGB inputs returned different pixels from
pinned Pillow 12.2.0.

Both decode paths also match libjpeg's replication rule when horizontally
subsampled chroma is only one or two samples wide. The full-plane dispatcher
now uses the same threshold as the row dispatcher. Direct baseline 4:2:2 and
4:2:0 paths delegate these tiny widths to the general reconstruction path;
raw RGB also uses the checked component assembler. Ordinary direct YCbCr paths
remain eligible for larger widths.

Progressive three-component output now uses reusable image-width scratch rows
instead of cropping and expanding two complete chroma planes. Full-resolution
rows are borrowed directly. Each component retains its own stride, visible
extent, and sampling ratios, and output/scratch reservations are fallible.
YCbCr rows still use the existing safe SIMD color converter; raw RGB rows are
interleaved directly. The baseline YCbCr full-plane fallback and its existing
fault contracts remain exercised.

Twenty-two new public decode parity rows cover tiny chroma widths, the
three-sample transition, minimal/odd/aligned RGB dimensions, both scan modes,
and the marker cases above. The original source passed only 6/22 of these rows.
The final selected campaign passed all 476 JPEG parity rows (343 decode and
133 encode), including 639 public encode calls and zero panics, plus all 13
existing JPEG fault contracts reported separately. The 64-case size/sampling
probe and 22 fixture probes also passed all 86 public decode executions,
representing 74 unique complete JPEGs. All 5,932 pre-existing input/output
reference rows are unchanged. No unit tests, fault contracts, coverage hooks,
or source exclusions were added.

Local Apple M3 Pro release measurements used Rust 1.96.1, an immutable saved
baseline executable, and the recorded dirty source identities. Three A-B-B-A
cycles measured complete public decode calls through owned output destruction
after 100 warmups per process. Input generation, file I/O, builds, and exact
comparisons were outside timing. All eight timed inputs passed full baseline,
candidate, and live Pillow pixel comparisons before timing. Incorrect raw RGB
and tiny-width baseline outputs were excluded from speed comparisons.

| Progressive RGB input, Q85 | Baseline median (ms) | Candidate median (ms) | Latency reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 128×128, 4:2:0 | 0.219729 | 0.203938 | 7.19% |

| 128×128, 4:2:2 | 0.323688 | 0.286584 | 11.46% |

Every progressive RGB cycle improved. The baseline RGB, progressive grayscale,

## Fractional JPEG sampling rejection parity — 2026-11-01

The decoder now rejects fractional component sampling ratios before pixel
reconstruction can truncate them through integer division. Previously, eight
baseline/progressive CMYK and YCbCr inputs with horizontal or vertical 3:2
ratios incorrectly decoded successfully; pinned Pillow 12.2.0 rejects their
pixel loads. Detection, header inspection, and verification remain successful,
matching Pillow. Valid integer 3:1 layouts still decode exactly.

Sixteen public decode parity rows pair those eight malformed inputs with
eight successful integer-ratio controls. Each complete 8×8 file has explicit
quantization/Huffman tables, zero-coefficient entropy, and EOI. SOF2 controls
contain an interleaved DC-first scan. Every MCU has at most ten blocks, so the
fractional cases isolate ratio acceptance rather than exceeding libjpeg's
interleaved MCU limit. The pinned generator
`generate_jpeg_sampling_ratio_fixtures.py --check` verifies complete file hashes,
header verification, successful pixels, and Pillow's fractional-load errors.
All 5,900 pre-existing input/output reference rows remain unchanged. No unit
tests, fault contracts, coverage hooks, or source exclusions were added.

The parser bounds component factors to 1 through 4. Maxima of one or two
therefore guarantee integer ratios; only larger layouts call the outlined
validator. A first inline guard and an unconditional outlined guard measured
10.84% and 9.21% higher RGB progressive decode medians respectively and were
rejected. Their sources, executables, and raw samples are retained. Rebuilding
the saved baseline produced a byte-identical benchmark executable.

Final local Apple M3 Pro controls used Rust 1.96.1 and three A-B-B-A cycles,
measuring complete public decode calls through output destruction after 100
warmups per process. Each of four 128×128 Q85 controls passed full baseline,
candidate, and live Pillow pixel comparisons before timing. The final controls
ranged from 0.14% lower to 1.29% higher median latency; RGB progressive decode
was 0.205750 ms versus 0.208396 ms. This bounds the local regression check,
without establishing zero overhead or a general speedup. Incorrect fractional
baseline outputs are excluded from timing comparisons.

integration binaries, with source and fixture identities unchanged throughout
execution. Native LLVM summary totals are 70.859518% lines, 63.117498% branches,
61.354098% functions, and 69.671003% regions. These are current local totals,
not a Coverage MCP incremental gain: imported reports remain source-unverified,
and the summary/detail reconciliation limitation described below remains.

## Explicit CMYK JPEG subsampling parity — 2026-11-01

Explicit CMYK 4:2:2 and 4:2:0 encoding now matches pinned Pillow 12.2.0
instead of silently writing 4:4:4. The first C component retains full
resolution; M, Y, and K use the requested sampling factors and the existing
downsampling filter. Unspecified CMYK sampling still defaults to 4:4:4.
The public sampling option documentation now explains that distinction.

The encoder fix exposed a second discrepancy: baseline and progressive CMYK
decoding replicated sampled components instead of applying IJG interpolation.
Both paths now share a checked, fallibly allocated output assembler. Sampled
images use four image-width scratch rows; unsampled images read borrowed
component rows directly. Horizontal 2:1 interpolation uses replication when
the component width is one or two samples, following the dispatch conditions
in the [pinned libjpeg-turbo source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/libjpeg-turbo/libjpeg-turbo/3.1.4.1/src/jdsample.c).
This narrow-width rule also applies to the existing shared YCCK row helper.

Nineteen ordinary encode parity cases cover both sampling layouts, optimized
and progressive output, restart rows, odd dimensions, partial MCU boundaries,
and single- and two-sample component widths. Three pinned lossless CMYK TIFF
sources provide varied K values, which the existing JPEG sources lack.
`generate_jpeg_cmyk_subsampling_fixture.py --check` verifies their complete
file and decoded-pixel hashes through the fixture-integrity target. All 5,862
pre-existing input/output reference rows remain unchanged. No unit tests or
target-only fault contracts were added.

The final selected campaign passed all 438 JPEG parity rows: 305 decode and
133 encode, exercising 639 public encode calls with zero panics. A separate
42-input public probe passed full-byte encode and decoded-pixel comparisons
against live Pillow for seven tiny dimensions, all three sampling layouts,
and baseline/progressive output. Retained intermediate failures distinguish
the original sampling discrepancy, the decoder interpolation discrepancy,
and the narrow-width dispatch discrepancy.

Local release controls compare the immutable preceding progressive-buffer
candidate with this candidate on the Apple M3 Pro, Rust 1.96.1. All four
128×128 Q85 RGB/CMYK baseline/progressive sources passed complete baseline,
candidate, and Pillow comparisons for both encoding and decoding before
timing. Three A-B-B-A cycles measured whole public calls through owned output
destruction after 100 warmups per process. Progressive CMYK 4:4:4 decoding
changed from 1.008667 ms to 0.876979 ms median latency (13.06% lower); all three
paired cycles improved. Encoding control medians ranged from 0.24% faster to
1.11% slower, and baseline CMYK decoding was 0.37% slower. The retained report
contains all eight controls, including RGB progressive decoding, which also
improved despite not being the targeted path. These observations do not
establish a universal speedup, an x86 runtime result, or a codec ranking.
Incorrect subsampled baseline outputs are excluded from timing comparisons.

## Progressive JPEG buffers and partial MCU parity — 2026-11-01

Progressive AC refinement now uses fixed 64-entry coefficient and correction
buffers instead of allocating temporary vectors for each block. A separate
correctness fix makes interleaved DC scans without restart markers retain
partial-MCU dummy blocks. These repeat the preceding DC value, contributing a
zero initial difference and its low refinement bit. The old path skipped them;
the varied 63×65 input produced 3,670 bytes versus Pillow's 3,675 bytes and
different decoded pixels. The corrected output matches Pillow byte for byte.

Three public encode parity rows cover bottom, right, and combined partial MCU
edges: `enc_progressive_bottom_partial_mcu_420`,
`enc_progressive_right_partial_mcu_420`, and `enc_progressive_partial_mcu_420`.
The first two use pinned deterministic RGB PNG sources at 63×65 and 65×63;
the third reuses the existing 33×33 JPEG. Existing input/output reference rows
are unchanged. All 114 JPEG encoder matrix rows passed, exercising 544 public
encode calls with zero panics. The new rows are ordinary Pillow parity cases;
no unit tests or target-only fault contracts were added.

## PNG zlib header and DEFLATE repeat rejection parity — 2026-11-01

Four ordinary PNG inputs retain the complete one-pixel RGB container, valid
chunk CRCs, and IEND. Pinned Pillow 12.2.0 accepts detection, inspection, and
structural verification, then rejects both still and sequence decoding:

| Public parity row | Input SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `decode:png:error_zlib_window_size_above_limit` | `85f3908b8187264634018450f6a3f7b75b82e62fee6f073b01141d78607f731b` |
| `decode:png:error_zlib_header_checksum_mismatch` | `e19795bb1425702730cfa038b17e2a2ed52556b63e3d01ceb054942aa2c0fb0c` |
| `decode:png:error_zlib_preset_dictionary` | `8bd1ca9a90c24d35a1048cc4fbfc90c0e397cbe42c1105370268c31699d84969` |
| `decode:png:error_zlib_dynamic_repeat_without_previous` | `499e28c39f5b6528ee9af60f0b4d953d7cbd14f4f7e3927074982114ba96c044` |

The window case keeps CM=8 and valid FCHECK while requesting a 64 KiB window.
The checksum case changes only FCHECK within IDAT and recomputes the PNG CRC.
The dictionary case contains a complete zlib stream that inflates to the source
raster when supplied its dictionary, which PNG forbids. The dynamic-tree case
uses a complete code-length alphabet but emits repeat symbol 16 before any
prior length. The dictionary case retains Pillow's `image file is truncated
(0 bytes not processed)` error; the other three retain its broken-stream error.
All four public rows passed their generated operation and structured-error
contracts in the selected Rust run (4/4, zero fault-contract rows).

Coverage MCP identified the unobserved header and repeat paths in the retained
full baseline. Raw LLVM branches at unchanged `deflate.rs` spans confirm the
following previously unobserved outcomes, each observed three times in the new
selection: excessive window (line 92, true), incorrect checksum (lines 93–97,
true), preset dictionary (line 98, true), and missing previous code length
(line 424, false). Both reports' local receipts match the current DEFLATE
source hash; zero-count duplicate mappings remain in the original reports.
These are selected-run observations, without managed source/test attribution
or a new whole-repository percentage.
Coverage MCP's incremental branch comparison returned `incomparable` because
the baseline details do not reconcile with its reported totals; the four raw
branch observations above are retained separately from that aggregate result.

`scripts/generate_png_deflate_header_edges.py --check` verifies all four
deterministic inputs through `make verify`; `--verify-pillow` also validates the
pinned oracle. Reference regeneration additionally repaired a stale generator
allow-list for four existing CDEF fault points already supported by the runner.
No production Rust source or unit tests were changed for these cases.

10-bit I420 key frame combining active luma CDEF with Wiener restoration.
Its 64-row height crosses the first 56-row restoration stripe boundary. This
checks the handoff between post-CDEF samples inside a stripe and saved
deblocked rows in its halo, with CDEF disabled for the chroma planes.

Pinned libavif 1.4.1/libaom 3.13.2 encodes are repeated and required to match.

`a6535b59e9da0eb66ee1bf768e080739bc8d88b2afc9554388b7620849900f1e`.
The generator pins CDEF damping 5, Y strength 47, UV strength 0, and one Wiener
luma restoration unit; no deblocking or super-resolution is enabled.

## AVIF metadata parity and preceding full coverage baseline — 2026-10-30

Added four public AVIF error cases. `error_avif_missing_meta` retains complete
`ftyp`/`mdat` boxes but omits `meta`. `error_avis_missing_moov` retains the
sequence's complete `ftyp`/`mdat`, omits `meta`/`moov`, and rewrites the
compatible `avif` brand to `avis` so the missing-movie condition is reached.

entry; Pillow opens it and fails while decoding frame zero. The generator pins
hashes, checks box layouts and unchanged AV1 media bytes, and verifies each
Pillow result.

## JPEG RGB 4:2:0 SSE2/AVX2 runtime comparison — 2026-10-26

The merged [PR #106](https://github.com/appunni-m/image-slash-star/pull/106)
added a 16-pixel RGB 4:2:0 conversion path for AVX2, while retaining the
existing SSE2 packet path. Its [x86 benchmark run](https://github.com/appunni-m/image-slash-star/actions/runs/40253085701)
completed five rounds for each of 40 JPEG encode/decode workloads on one
AVX2-capable Ubuntu host. The SSE2 lane ran before the AVX2 lane. All 40 Rust
output lengths and hashes matched across the two builds.

For RGB Q85 4:2:0 encoding, the recorded median was 159,989 ns under SSE2 and
123,933 ns under AVX2 at 128x128 (1.291x), 3,340,953 ns and 2,830,304 ns at
512x512 (1.181x), and 13,394,850 ns and 11,414,454 ns at 1024x1024 (1.174x).
In the same artifact, AVX2 Rust medians were 1.417x, 1.684x, and 1.729x the
TurboJPEG 3.2.0 medians for those workloads. These hosted sequential runs show
an AVX2-over-SSE2 improvement for the sampled workload, while leaving a clear
gap to the oracle; they do not support a fastest-in-the-world or project-wide
claim. The retained [benchmark artifact](https://github.com/appunni-m/image-slash-star/actions/runs/40253085701/artifacts/12621916274)
has SHA-256 `fecb3cf22f5f92a1da9c825a05ae010bf5be21af02f50a4e3b3c836d0ee44aeb`.


## AVIF I420 chroma reuse — 2026-10-28

The public `decode_sequence` profile for
`animated_motion_temporal_mv_range_2048x128.avif` showed substantial time in
the scalar 4:2:0 chroma filter. The decoder now advances row and column
coordinates without per-pixel division, shares U/V filter geometry, and reuses
each vertically filtered chroma sample across its adjacent output columns.
The fixed-point weights, pre-filter high-depth shift, edge replication, and
single final rounding operation are preserved. No unsafe code or unit tests
were added.

On an Apple M3 Pro running macOS 15.7.7 with Rust 1.96.1, paired A–B–B–A runs
timed the complete public sequence decode and output destruction 42 times per
run in locked release builds (`--no-default-features --features avif`). The
checkout was based on `69a79d4c4`, with locked dependencies and matching
release settings; the only codec-source change between the A/B builds was
`src/codecs/avif/decode.rs`. The fixture SHA-256 is
`294468c2498c8fa494bfcc2e701a944e90f15ec4b5f08eb64fa34f907e5a6a1a`, and the
decoded output totals 2,359,296 RGB bytes. Baseline medians were 14.953 ms and
14.865 ms; the optimized medians were 12.238 ms and 12.194 ms. Averaging the
two run medians gives an 18.06% latency reduction. This is one AVIF decode
workload, not an encoder result or an x86 runtime result. A portable eight-lane
RGB conversion experiment passed parity but did not improve the paired
end-to-end result, so it was removed. `make lint-x86-simd` confirms the
retained source still compiles under SSE2 and AVX2 flags; it does not measure
runtime speed on those CPUs.

The final selected parity run passed seven public rows spanning 4:2:0 and
4:2:2, odd dimensions, 10-bit and 12-bit samples, alpha, and the timed
animation. Coverage MCP found no missing branch coordinates in the new
vertical-geometry or cached-sampling helpers for that run. The report is
`.coverage-mcp/local-evidence/selected/avif-420-filter-cache-final-20261028/coverage.json`
(SHA-256
`406fa5e215d8b347b4a1b2b7f1cf86533f7e18ae47b366b7d5f70bc55fb20896`). Its
source/build identity and test attribution are unverified by Coverage MCP, so
this is selected coordinate evidence, not an aggregate coverage claim. Timing
logs are retained under
`.coverage-mcp/local-evidence/perf/avif-sequence-2048x128-arm64/`.

## PNG chunk iterator failed-state contract — 2026-10-27

## WebP hash-chain index guard contract — 2026-10-27

Added the target-only contract
`fault-contract:webp:webp_hash_chain_index_overflow_rejected` for the private
VP8L hash-chain index bound. Public WebP encoding caps each axis at 16,384
pixels, so a Pillow parity input cannot exceed the `i32` sample-index range.
The `cfg(coverage)` fault point drives this defensive guard through the public
encoder while leaving release builds without fault controls.

The case first decodes the active Pillow `lossless_vp8l` input, injects the
failure, and checks the structured WebP `Dimensions` error. An uninjected
retry must match the existing `enc_lossless` Pillow byte reference, produce
the same bytes as a fresh retry, and decode to the Pillow RGB reference. The
range check now runs once before the low-effort/high-effort const-generic split.
In the focused run, both outcomes of the `i32` conversion check were observed;
Coverage MCP reports no missing branch at that guard. The selected run passed
1/1. Its report is
`.coverage-mcp/local-evidence/selected/webp-hash-chain-index-overflow-20261027-attempt-3/coverage.json`

## AVIF qindex-zero non-lossless inter parity — 2026-10-27

Added active rows
`decode:avif:animated_lossy_inter_420_b16x64_qindex0_mode_select_64x64` and
`decode:avif:animated_lossy_inter_monochrome_b16x64_qindex0_mode_select_64x64`.
Both deterministic 64×64 sequences use a lossless key frame and a non-lossless
qindex-zero `TX_MODE_SELECT` inter frame. The I420 inter frame has chroma
quantizer deltas of 2; the monochrome inter frame has a luma DC delta of 2.

frame headers, and exact Pillow RGB frame hashes.

the segment non-lossless. This avoids consuming a transform-type symbol that
these inputs do not signal. The focused public parity run passed 2/2, with
12,288 RGB bytes matching Pillow for each case. The full `make test` run also
passed, including the complete matrix suite and native, WASI, and WASM feature
lanes. The local LLVM report is

## TIFF packed-tile bit-order dispatch — 2026-10-25

Coverage MCP previously reported opposite unobserved arms for `if LSB_FIRST`
inside the two boolean-const-generic packed-row specializations. A valid TIFF
input could select one specialization, but could never take the other
specialization's impossible arm. Replaced those conditionals with statically
dispatched `PackedTileBitOrder` implementations for most-significant-first and
least-significant-first samples. Their optimized per-sample methods are marked
`inline(always)` so orientation dispatch does not add calls to the inner loop.

methods. This checks code generation for that target; it is not an end-to-end
benchmark or SSE2/AVX2 performance result.

## WebP VP8 method-zero sampling parity — 2026-10-20

Corrected libwebp parity in VP8 coefficient adaptation: method 0 samples the
first 50 macroblocks through 200 macroblocks, then samples one quarter of the
frame; skip probability uses the full frame macroblock count. Token-buffer
methods no longer signal skip probability, and an Intra4 macroblock skipped
after zero residuals preserves the Y2 contexts as libwebp does. These changes
reuse the existing macroblock decisions and add no extra per-macroblock pass.

## ICO/CUR entry-selection parity — 2026-10-20

Added five active Pillow parity rows covering ICO directory selection and CUR
hotspot handling: equal-area lower-depth preference, stable equal-depth ties,
both zero-bit-count depth fallbacks, equal-size CUR entries with different
y-hotspots, and a CUR entry whose width and height both increase. The CUR
equal-size witness uses a 1x11 canvas, keeping y-hotspots 10 and 2 in bounds.
The larger-dimensions CUR witness orders a 1x1 green entry before a 2x2 red
entry and confirms Pillow selects the later entry.

The ICO decoder and inspector now share area-then-depth selection for ICOs,
including Pillow's palette-derived `ceil(log2(color_count))` fallback and the
maximum-depth fallback when the palette count is absent. CUR selection follows
Pillow's raw directory rule: a later entry replaces the current one only when
both raw dimensions are strictly larger. ICO bit-depth bytes are not treated
as CUR hotspot coordinates.

## JPEG marker-tail and YCCK singleton parity — 2026-10-20

Added active Pillow-backed rows
`decode:jpeg:baseline_444_single_scan_com_tail_junk`,
`decode:jpeg:baseline_444_single_scan_com_eoi_marker_fill`,
`decode:jpeg:baseline_444_single_scan_com_ff00_tail`,
`decode:jpeg:baseline_444_single_scan_two_trailing_com`, and
`decode:jpeg:ycck_h2v2_single_sample_1x1`. The COM-tail rows derive from the
8×8 baseline COM control by inserting a `00` junk byte, a legal `FF`
marker-fill byte, or an `FF00` stuffed pair before EOI; the fourth case adds a
second valid COM segment before EOI. Pillow 12.2.0 verifies and decodes all
four to the control's same 192 RGB bytes. The FF00 candidate SHA-256 is
`7ee7bd8d0fd0734f5b51cc0cd29e8fae262b29f0d6366ab5dcf081ea787e5dc3`;
its pinned base SHA-256 is
`cf8e4443dcff4df7858b6573664aa3fe73dd401827aa293d0eca84eb0667f666`. The YCCK
case changes only the SOF0 dimensions from 2×2 to 1×1; Pillow returns one CMYK
pixel, `ff ff fd ff`. The second-COM candidate SHA-256 is
`c23f18f246085b1b088d82f9c660e1939d9d3198dda3c05ea5fe1dcf961a78e8`.

The COM-tail rows exposed that the baseline decoder's validated single-scan
fast path rejected bytes after a trailing marker, then sent the valid scan
through generic extraction with the post-scan marker bytes included as entropy.
It now skips intervening bytes and FF00 stuffed pairs only after a valid
allow-listed trailing segment and bounds repeated marker-fill scanning at
parsed EOI. `parse_jpeg` guarantees the initial cursor is at an FF marker, so
the previously uncovered pre-segment non-marker guard was unreachable for
parser-produced input and was removed instead of adding an artificial test.
This preserves the entropy boundary and accepts the Pillow-observable inputs.

The exact selected regression run passed 7/7 rows on `aarch64-apple-darwin`
with all features and branch instrumentation, including the existing trailing
COM control and DQT marker-fill case:

```text
PYTHON=.oracle-venv/bin/python make coverage-selected COVERAGE_CASES='decode:jpeg:baseline_444_single_scan_trailing_com decode:jpeg:baseline_444_single_scan_com_tail_junk decode:jpeg:baseline_444_single_scan_com_eoi_marker_fill decode:jpeg:baseline_444_single_scan_com_ff00_tail decode:jpeg:baseline_444_single_scan_two_trailing_com decode:jpeg:baseline_444_single_scan_dqt_marker_fill decode:jpeg:ycck_h2v2_single_sample_1x1' SELECTED_COVERAGE_REPORT=.coverage-mcp/local-evidence/20261020/jpeg-tail-parity-seven/coverage.json
```

the reciprocal bound. The arbitrary-i32 quantizer retained its correction.

rows (379 calls, zero panics), 205/205 decode rows, and all 20 complete-byte
baseline/candidate output comparisons before each timing campaign.

#### Capacity-growth-only allocation contract

`avif_retained_temporal_sample_reservation_failure` is a separate target-only
case using ordinary `animated_motion_multitile_split_groups`. Its
`av1.frame.retained_temporal_sample_reservation` hook consumes only when a
partial group's nonempty sample count exceeds spare vector capacity. Empty
or already-fitting groups cannot consume it. `usize::MAX` additional
nonzero-sized samples causes an actual deterministic `try_reserve` capacity
failure without host OOM. Normal builds retain the actual sample request,

frame's public pixels without providing a witness for the older square helper.

the upper bound for the fixed `[u32; 4]` arrays; the guard now uses each array's

### AV1 film-grain parity and restoration fault contracts — 2026-10-05

The public parity row `decode:avif:animated_filmgrain_reference_reuse_i444_64x64`
uses a two-frame full-resolution I444 sequence. The first key frame refreshes
film-grain parameters into reference slot 0; the second displayed inter frame
sets `update=false`, reuses slot 0, and supplies a new seed. Pinned Pillow
12.2.0/libavif 1.4.1 decodes both frames. The selected Rust parity run passed
1/1, including exact per-frame pixel references.

The public row
`decode:avif:portable_lossless_filmgrain_420_chroma_from_luma_64x64` adds a
lossless I420 key frame with `chroma_scaling_from_luma=true`, non-empty Y
scaling points, and empty U/V point arrays. The generator preserves the tile
payload and item extent, validates the rewritten syntax with the independent
OBU inspector, and pins the exact Pillow RGB output. Its selected Rust parity
run passed 1/1. Coverage MCP reports no remaining branch gap at the
`read_film_grain` chroma-scaling gate (`frame.rs:4277`) in the full AVIF matrix.

The public row
`decode:avif:portable_lossless_filmgrain_420_zero_y_points_64x64` exercises a
valid 8-bit I420 key frame whose film-grain syntax has `num_y_points == 0` and
CFL disabled. AV1 infers empty U/V point tables and omits luma AR coefficients
for this 4:2:0 syntax. The deterministic generator preserves the tile payload
and item extent, validates the rewritten OBU independently, and pins Pillow's
exact 12,288-byte RGB output
(`5d35ab50438b9f1536ef7de3cbca8ac3d01360efa9d77446dfe0d69786d2fb62`).
The selected public parity row passed 1/1. The decoder now accepts this legal
case, retains a zero luma-grain LUT for active chroma consumers, and skips Y
plane writes when no Y points are present. With no active chroma points, it
returns after geometry and parameter validation without allocating grain LUTs.

This case exposed an admission gap: lossless non-super-resolution inter
reconstruction rejected all film-grain frames before producing a color
surface. The decoder now admits only bounded full-resolution I444 grain for
that lossless profile. Grain remains display-only and retained reference
samples remain ungrained. The bounded geometry and depth checks match the
existing display materializer.

The target-only row
`fault-contract:avif:avif_sgr_intermediate_reservation_failure` injects a
deterministic reservation failure in SGR intermediate allocation while
decoding the active
`decode:avif:animated_lossy_inter_420_superres_sgr_8bit_160x56` input. It

### JPEG bulk entropy refill experiment rejected — 2026-11-04

Native x86 A-B-B-A run 41812150890 compared baseline `3607da286639c16a0cf76c32f09fffcdf8b675be` with the committed candidate from PR head `11a4fdf4c3479416ab2f38c86709d36abc4c0ed9`. Six primary cohorts completed on both SSE2 and AVX2, and the benchmark's output-identity checks passed. The candidate failed the performance gate: SSE2 primary paired gain was -2.0854% with a -2.6305% minimum guard gain; AVX2 primary paired gain was -4.9570% with a -4.9859% minimum guard gain. Zero of six primary cohorts were faster on either variant.

The largest cases regressed on both variants. SSE2 grayscale 512x512 4:2:0 moved from 2.560 ms to 2.612 ms and 4:2:2 from 2.560 ms to 2.631 ms. AVX2 moved from 2.209 ms to 2.320 ms and from 2.203 ms to 2.317 ms, respectively. Reject the bulk refill implementation and retain the byte-at-a-time reader. Keep the separately validated marker-prefix EOF fault contract; its `cfg(coverage)` hook is absent from production builds.

## Selected parity and coverage — 2026-10-03

The JPEG public decode matrix passes 174/174 active rows, including valid cases
where Cb and Cr use different sampling factors. Those cases exposed a panic in
the generic reconstruction path: it cropped Cr using Cb's plane dimensions.
Reconstruction now crops and upsamples each chroma plane from its own sampling
factors. The existing baseline 4:2:0, 4:2:2, 4:4:4, grayscale, and CMYK direct
decoders still return before this generic path.

The four selected `baseline_420_chroma_component_sampling_fallback` rows pass
4/4. Their LLVM report is
`target/release-evidence/coverage-jpeg-chroma-component-sampling-all-variants-20261003.json`.
Coverage MCP's older full report showed missing true arms for the Cb/Cr
horizontal and vertical sampling guards at `decode.rs:1170-1173`; the selected
report now observes those true arms. The false arm at line 1173 remains
uncovered in that selected run. This is coordinate evidence from reports with
no source/build receipts; MCP lists test attribution as unknown.

The same full report has a PNG chunk-iterator stop observation. Its raw LLVM
branch table identifies the missing arm as `Chunks::failed`; the position-at-EOF
arm is already exercised by the active missing-IEND input. Every public chunk
consumer propagates a chunk error immediately, so none requests another item
after `failed` becomes true. TIFF's packed-tile extent checks follow validated
tile geometry and bounded source rows. BMP signature guards and ICO size guards
are preempted by public dispatch/source validation; reaching the BMP file-size
limit with a valid image would require impractically large pixel storage. These
remain defensive branches without valid public Pillow parity witnesses, rather
than reasons to add private coverage-only tests.

`encode_six_coefficient_major_edge_raw_blocks` helper also receives chroma

The JPEG direct-decoder bailout audit found a valid baseline multi-scan edge:
Pillow accepts a 4:4:4 image that encodes Cb, Y, and Cr in separate
non-interleaved sequential scans. The active
`baseline_444_three_sequential_scans` fixture is generated by splitting a
single 8×8 interleaved Pillow JPEG. The resulting file has SHA-256
`b9e3e277c0d05b2df169804236d5f9b72d3a1c8beda33e845f9c6ffd436f424b`, and its
decoded pixels match the original Pillow JPEG exactly (pixel SHA-256
`0d4dccc69dc0ee4ae956be8c624186ddb2b5f3d411671361056c51a7ea7f9e66`). The
active `baseline_444_three_scans_dqt_redefined` variant inserts a new
8-bit Cb quantization table between the first and second scans. Pillow's
decoded pixels differ from the original when the final table changes (input
SHA-256 `74d02103e151831846019cbcf009f2d17912988045e8d82e850828e18d1724f7`,
pixel SHA-256
`983025493b251f11b379bbbf15a92cde4e5b9177e63626ff035e0049cc6779b4`), so
each component latches its quantization table at its first scan; scans retain
their SOS Huffman and restart settings. The decoder handles non-interleaved
block geometry and resets DC predictors at scan and restart boundaries.
Single-scan baseline decoding keeps its existing dispatch and fast paths, and
the parser defers per-scan table copies until a later scan or table update
requires them.

Coverage MCP surfaced three additional Pillow-tolerated SOF0 cases. The
`baseline_444_multiscan_ss_nonzero` row sets Ss to 1 in the first sequential
scan; Pillow returns the same pixels as the ordinary three-scan input (input
SHA-256 `7a36ce48ba3d15bcefb15ad70b1a5e3f0c70523c84d2cdadade2ed6531e0094d`, pixel SHA-256
`0d4dccc69dc0ee4ae956be8c624186ddb2b5f3d411671361056c51a7ea7f9e66`).
`baseline_444_multiscan_duplicate_component` changes the final scan's component
ID from Cr to the already-seen Cb (input SHA-256
`76b4d1d36238ff9f92d63a44bb6dc1bcde040e99e0217f15b1c96f4a624668cc`, pixel
SHA-256 `2b73ccd3b62ddd2c645e63cd0d65ed016fc25a461d82e161514ac0d48fb2fb52`).
Pillow maps that scan back to Cb and leaves the omitted Cr plane neutral. Its
coefficient buffer retains earlier AC values where a repeated sequential scan
encodes zeros, so the Rust path stores coefficient history only for components
that repeat and merges the later block coefficients. This follows libjpeg-turbo's
multiscan coefficient buffers and Huffman decoder ([`jdcoefct.c`](https://github.com/libjpeg-turbo/libjpeg-turbo/blob/main/src/jdcoefct.c),
[`jdhuff.c`](https://github.com/libjpeg-turbo/libjpeg-turbo/blob/main/src/jdhuff.c)).
The `baseline_444_multiscan_missing_component` row omits the final Cr scan and
leaves its neutral plane initialized (input SHA-256
`d91a46924a2310aae6a9b7c16fd7f091eaf21bff8a8b74dc99c388d1983e6a8a`, pixel
SHA-256 `669b0f32cd296cd0742d7e9b8e9c25cf7a4f114b6a5788f83af5ed0e89f409b7`).
The `baseline_444_multiscan_empty_entropy` row removes the first component
scan's entropy while retaining its SOS; Pillow accepts the file and leaves that

`f8bba1d8f8e8f631f5487349550f64a3bd3438a9789ed293619d7e2553be6192`, pixel
SHA-256 `1b343e02a958d0137fd239618dd0332265457fc011296714fe1a42cf0e35d49d`).
`baseline_444_multiscan_interleaved_restart` combines Y and Cb in one scan,
leaves Cr in a singleton scan, and places a restart marker between its two
MCUs (input SHA-256
`ddbcf29eb1549aae0356661ff2b879b7b2b23b7aae924adbb424af22246e20d7`, pixel
SHA-256 `f83545d43c6939ec393b6b8310959b6174fd764b08a12fc22d908408a7e6a43e`).
The `baseline_444_multiscan_restart_overrun` variant adds two trailing restart
markers; the first creates an empty segment after the final MCU. Pillow accepts

`1aac34523a7e6491744764d84c9c0de21ef9a308d532924e121c7c36229defe6`, pixel

Rust matches all 49,152 Pillow bytes. The selected public matrix row passes
1/1. Its LLVM branch report changes the targeted arm from zero observations
for `decode:jpeg:subsampling_444` to four observations for the new row. The
Coverage MCP selected-test comparison reports the line-410 arm as newly
observed, but remains limited because source/build receipts are absent. The
selected report is `target/jpeg-coverage-probe/coverage-public-row.json`; this
is coordinate-level evidence, not a full-suite coverage claim.

## JPEG direct-safe SOF component-count invariant — 2026-10-04

Coverage MCP also showed missing true arms for `components.len() != N` in the
grayscale, CMYK, 4:2:0, 4:2:2, and 4:4:4 baseline direct-safe paths. Those arms
are unreachable from public JPEG inputs: `parse_sof0` builds the component
vector from the SOF count, the parser derives `num_components` from that vector,
and its sole `JpegInfo` construction stores both values together. The five
redundant hot-path checks were removed and the invariant is documented on
`JpegInfo`; no private unit tests or coverage exclusions were added. The public
JPEG decode matrix passes 203/203 rows. The selected LLVM report is
`target/release-evidence/coverage-jpeg-direct-safe-guards-20261004.json`; MCP
has no source/build receipts, so it is row-local evidence and does not support
a verified aggregate coverage-gain claim.

`decode_inter_translation_impl` and `decode_following_vertical`; specialization
counts are not distinct source branches. A selected run of the clipped
`animated_lossless_inter_420_clipped_b32x32_64x60` row passes public parity and
reaches the true outcome at lines 54836–54838 in one of eight compiled
`decode_inter_translation_impl` specializations. Its report has no source/build
receipts, so retain this as coordinate evidence.

The 32×32 `animated_lossless_inter_420_b32x32_10bit` row records no branch

records 14,277/32,072 branches (44.52%) for that earlier matrix. It predates

could not calculate an incremental union with the earlier report because exact
baseline branch detail is incomplete, so no marginal percentage gain is

## Packed low-bit TIFF tiles — 2026-10-02

conformance.

## Separate-planar TIFF parity — 2026-10-02

Manifest parity now covers PlanarConfiguration 2 RGB strips and tiles, including
raw data, Deflate with and without horizontal prediction, partial right/bottom
tiles, missing final strips and tiles that Pillow zero-fills, one-sample
grayscale, and 1:1 YCbCr strips and tiles. The YCbCr cases preserve Pillow's raw
component triplets in RGB mode. Malformed rows cover excess strip/tile offsets,
out-of-bounds strip/tile payloads, zero rows per strip, invalid planar value 3,
and missing, empty, zero, or mismatched compressed byte counts. Pillow accepts
inspection for invalid planar value 3 but fails at pixel load; Rust matches that
lazy failure. Pillow also rejects extra separate-planar tile offsets during
open, while a short final raw tile remains a successful zero-filled decode.

At that measurement, the TIFF decode matrix passed all 161 active rows. The full
`make coverage` campaign passes all suites and repository floors with
`target/release-evidence/coverage-full-planar-tiles-20261002.json`: 84,990/141,861
lines (59.91%), 15,994/32,130 branches (49.78%), 4,768/8,959 functions

diagnostic rather than source-bound claims. The current matrix has 1,367 active
decode rows and 392 active encode rows at that point. Strict debug, release,
coverage-configured, x86-64 SSE2-baseline, and AVX2 Clippy checks pass. The x86
SIMD commands are compile checks and do not measure runtime performance.

`pillow_tolerated_post_idat_color_chunks` appends PLTE and tRNS chunks after

`apng_orphan_fdat_missing_control` keeps the orphaned `fdAT` sequence number

## TIFF YCbCr LZW parity — 2026-10-17

The public TIFF matrix adds three Pillow 12.2.0 inputs for contiguous 8-bit
YCbCr with default 2-by-2 subsampling: the 4×4 Kata candidate, a 3×3 image
that clips the right and bottom clump edges while omitting default tags 530
and 531, and a 4×4 image split across two aligned LZW strips with centered
positioning. Their input SHA-256 values are respectively
`d9c3e4b7111658f3b86fdb1f94bf04e03aebe7cb4fbd01a98708ebfd27e65a6c`,
`67df0dce7b4cab6af8d43f258f7eb1b77ba119e096ad242083baec83ebd585e9`, and
`1dd542a0a6e22d922f66e0f19e92421dd15fd1108f726af38810a11a6bf13487`.
An additional full-resolution 1-by-1 LZW row guards the compressed path while
the existing uncompressed 1-by-1 rows retain Pillow's RGBX raw behavior; its
input SHA-256 is `c3ebf5fdd35da227f9ef92cf45b81d726c908a0be1fe3e52c1bd3abfe699f9b6`.
The 32×32 subsampled control reaches the conversion loop's 1,024-pixel
cancellation checkpoint; its input and RGB reference hashes are
`655b9b0172e44433b222cc93acdd2e14ca296e22f373e5f073e2e24d33b5111f` and
`c5fc0bdafed814b597605fb7d00ce7510c60e1b45e774d0c71c4850ec39b4ded`.

The Kata candidate is 186 bytes and decodes to the exact Pillow RGB byte
sequence recorded in `scripts/generate_tiff_ycbcr_subsampled_fixtures.py`
(SHA-256 `af15457a9372a158dd276ced4109b650b99def573093a49f70dbb469c2262668`).
For compressed full-resolution data, the decoder converts each YCbCr triple;
the four 2-by-2 cases read six-byte clumps (`Y00,Y01,Y10,Y11,Cb,Cr`), check
clump and output geometry with checked arithmetic, clip odd image edges, and
apply libtiff's fixed-point default conversion. Libtiff's RGBA path applies a
clump's chroma to all four luma samples for either legal positioning value.
The subsampled layout supports contiguous strips with predictor 1 and aligned
two-row strip boundaries. Uncompressed files retain Pillow's RGBX raw path,
including the existing 1-by-1 rows. The fixture generator pins input hashes,
tag claims, and oracle output hashes, and is part of `make verify`.

The active `ycbcr_subsampled_lzw_1x2` row adds Pillow-compatible horizontal
full-resolution and vertical 2:1 subsampling. Its 203-byte complete TIFF has
input SHA-256
`d659443b0f3eb3c6de349a45d3e007e482b6727c4682f82545df0ac5b49971c9`; pinned
Pillow 12.2.0 decodes it to 4×4 RGB with reference SHA-256
`1ddadfe41e070962f7991dda8e8d26efc8c43a7352227b45154387a9991c5fb6`. Rust
accepts `[1, 2]` subsampling and keeps the established `[2, 2]` converter on its
existing specialized path. The selected public parity row passes. Two separate
target-only fault-contract rows exercise clump-length rejection and RGB output
reservation failure on the 1-by-2 path; both declare Pillow `not_applicable`
and are reported outside the parity totals.

The active `ycbcr_subsampled_lzw_1x2_odd_height` row is a 4×3, 203-byte TIFF
with the same 1-by-2 LZW layout. Its input SHA-256 is
`00013d30c2155603f592722acf82b52154eb031774453023612d93a8983e2185`; pinned
Pillow produces 36 RGB bytes with SHA-256
`c71479e1cfff0dd7c76fbe5df2c61e80c75405df52c1aa2413e2f4d08a99f1fb`. It
reaches and passes the new converter's bottom-edge clipping condition. The

The AVIF compound-reference investigation found a CDF table-axis error that
could panic on a valid context-2 stream. The correction indexes each CDF by
branch group then context. A deterministic full-file AVIF mutation preserves
the compound-reference prefix and damages only a later coded sample; Pillow
and Rust both reject sequence decoding as malformed, while the first image
still matches Pillow exactly. An isolated public `decode_sequence` trace stops
at the corrected backward-reference CDF lookup with group 0/context 2; the old
transposed access would index beyond that table's two group rows. The selected
parity row then returns its structured malformed result. This access occurs in
an earlier AV1 sample than the mutation at byte 16098, so it proves the public
prefix exercises the fix but does not attribute the eventual sequence error to
the changed byte or frame. The valid DIFFWTD stream still reaches other AV1
decoder limitations, so it is not counted as a successful parity case.

Two local release A/B runs per source version exercised the public JPEG
benchmark matrix on an Apple M3 Pro, with three alternating rounds per run.
Across 63×65, 127×129, 128², 512², and 1024² RGB 4:2:0 encodes, the median of
the run medians was 5.3–7.8% lower after the MCU-check cleanup; Rust output
lengths and hashes matched before and after in all five cases. One baseline run
started with a 1-minute load average of 10.7, so these are directional local
measurements rather than a cross-machine or release speed claim.

A separate release profile used the public Rust runner for a 1024×1024 RGB
4:2:0 encode (2,000 measured iterations after 100 warmups) on the same M3 Pro.
The median was 6.806 ms and P95 was 7.200 ms. A five-second `sample` capture
recorded 3,866 stacks; `rgb_to_ycbcr_420_packet` appeared in 340 stacks (8.8%)
and the four-block FDCT in 221 (5.7%). This is a single-workload diagnostic
that points to color conversion for follow-up profiling. It is not a paired
speedup measurement, and it provides no SSE2 or AVX2 runtime evidence.

A same-checkout A/B isolated `#[inline(always)]` on
`rgb_to_ycbcr_420_packet`. Seven alternating release-runner pairs on the M3 Pro
measured 128², 512², and 1024² RGB 4:2:0 encodes. The candidate medians were
2.61%, 0.34%, and 3.18% lower, respectively; every encoded length and hash
matched. These small local gains support retaining the hint. The run does not
measure SSE2 or AVX2 execution. Raw paired results are in the ignored local
artifact `target/benchmarks/jpeg/goal-continuation-2026-09-29/packet-inline-controlled-ab.json`.

of 1.0067 versus baseline; RGB 512² and 1024² 4:2:0 encodes regressed 5.15% and

evidence only, not an SSE2 or AVX2 runtime measurement. The local candidate
report is `target/benchmarks/jpeg/goal-20261001-arm64-3load-candidate`.

`decode_inter_translation_impl` observations across specializations. The
apparent lossy I422 narrow path requires transform mode 0 and a non-lossless

fixture; no parity row should be invented to exercise it. A separate reachable
candidate is diff-weighted compound prediction at `block.rs:57292` and
`:57310`. No candidate is accepted without independent syntax inspection and
exact Pillow/native frame parity.

The JPEG quantizer now omits its upward quotient correction: prepared JPEG
divisors are 8–2040 and use `ceil(2^32 / divisor)`, so multiply-high cannot
underestimate the quotient. The single downward correction remains, and the
public JPEG encode parity matrix passes all 61 active rows. Ten alternating
500-encode captures of the public 1024×1024 RGB quality-85 4:2:0 workload on an
Apple M3 Pro measured a 1.14% lower median of run medians (6.271 ms candidate,
6.343 ms baseline); six of ten paired runs were faster. Output size and FNV-1a
hash were identical at 793,139 bytes and `d748543a168ce6aa`. This is a small,
directional ARM64 result; raw records are in
`target/benchmarks/jpeg/goal-quantizer-20261002/`, and no x86 runtime speedup is
claimed.

for I444 right and bottom edges, I422 right-edge cases, and I422/I444 dual-edge cases. The new
`animated_lossless_inter_i444_clipped_b32x32_64x56.avif` has SHA-256
`9004ec840b2a413c0e15294f52c723ebe5c3689cbe3decbd4afd5575cad78e23`; its

20x32 clipped right block. The two 52x60 dual-edge cases pass exact sequence
parity with 20x28 luma visibility; I422 chroma visibility is 10x28. For odd-width I422 at 49x64, key-frame pixels match
Pillow and sequence decoding keeps an explicit `Unsupported` expectation
because the final chroma sample geometry is not parity-safe. The AVIF matrix
now has 454 active decode rows; the full fixture matrix has 1,950 rows.

`make coverage` passed all executed tests and the local floors. Its LLVM report

`parse_iloc::<true>` hook (`samples.rs:1095`). Both reports are selected-only;
MCP labels source identity unverified and test attribution unknown. The full
baseline comparison is incomparable because its exact branch detail is
incomplete, so no aggregate gain or regression is claimed. No full coverage
campaign ran. Reports and receipts are in
`.coverage-mcp/local-evidence/20261013/avif-iinf-parity/` and
`.coverage-mcp/local-evidence/20261013/avif-metadata-fault-contracts-selected/`.

`make fmt` and `make verify` pass; strict all-feature Clippy passed with
`RUSTC_WRAPPER=` after the default `sccache` wrapper was denied by the local
sandbox. The broad asset command
`.oracle-venv/bin/python scripts/generate_test_assets.py --format avif` still
stops at its existing pinned ICC fixture-hash check before reaching the new

with the single-field mutation and verified against the recorded digest.

## Diagnostic provenance

The separate defensive-model contract has 61 diagnostic cases: 38 use committed bytes that also have a Pillow parity row;
23 cases construct runtime mutations. Diagnostic identities and messages remain
Rust model observations, not Pillow parity fields. The provenance verifier checks
the original input hashes and supporting baseline route for every case.

## Contract catalog: behavior Pillow cannot prove

This is the separate Rust-only list. “Cannot prove” means Pillow may have a
similar idea internally, but it cannot return this crate's exact field, token,
target, sink, or typed result for comparison.

The bounded v1 map is machine-checked by
`make verify` against
`tests/fixtures/unreachable_contract_manifest.json`. `covered` means that the
manifest names an existing fixture-backed integration contract or fixture
verifier; `planned` means that no such contract is claimed yet. The map is an
evidence index, not a claim that every legal format state is implemented.

The verifier also parses this ten-row table. It requires each row's status and
Pillow-parity column to match the manifest, every covered row to name the exact
manifest evidence paths, the release-package row to name its exact fixture
verifier, and the planned allocation/stack/coverage row to say that no
category-specific evidence is claimed while naming its bounded context paths.
This is documentation-integrity evidence only: it does not promote the planned
category to covered and does not add any Rust-only result to Pillow parity.

The separate `fault_contract_cases` index maps target-only injected failures
and defensive parser branches to their structured-diagnostics requirement and shared matrix selector. The
AVIF, BMP, JPEG, and TIFF fault cases reuse active Pillow parity inputs as
reproducible stimulus, while each injected result is recorded with
`verification: fault-contract` and `oracle_status: not_applicable`. The new AVIF
monochrome alpha case shortens one sample only under `cfg(coverage)`, expects
`NotImplemented` at `StillDecode`, and compares a clean retry with a fresh
decode. It is target-only diagnostic evidence, not Pillow parity. The runner
reports this lane separately from Pillow decode/encode counts. The TIFF ignored-sample contracts exercise zero row bytes and a short assembled buffer. The TIFF YCbCr contracts also exercise zero horizontal and vertical subsampling after valid-layout selection, then verify a clean Pillow-parity retry. The YCbCr
cases force clump-length failures in the 1-by-2, 2-by-2, and general
converters, full-resolution sample-length failures, and RGB-output reservation
failures in the 1-by-2, 2-by-2, and general converters. They assert the
expected typed decode error followed by a successful retry against the same
Pillow-backed input.

Rust-only results do not belong in Pillow parity rows. The shared matrix has a
separate `fault_contracts` lane for deterministic target-internal failures and
defensive parser branches that public API routing cannot exercise. Each such
row is typed as `fault-contract`, uses `oracle_status: not_applicable`, and
shares the matrix selector and case-index machinery without contributing to
parity counts. Its input may be an existing Pillow parity fixture; that keeps
the stimulus reproducible but does not turn the target-only result into Pillow
parity. The PNG signature inspection contract decodes the 1×1 Pillow fixture,
flips one signature bit on a copy under `cfg(coverage)`, then calls the codec
inspector directly and checks its structured malformed result. Public format
detection rejects that copied input before dispatch, so the defensive check
cannot be exercised by the public parity row.

### AVIF monochrome group-buffer allocation fault contract — 2026-10-15

`fault-contract:avif:avif_monochrome_group_buffer_reservation_failure` reuses
the active `decode:avif:multitile_monochrome` Pillow parity input. The fixture
reaches the per-tile-group complete-monochrome buffer reservation, while the
coverage-only fault point forces its fallible reserve to report a structured
`Dimensions` error. The public fault-contract runner checks the AVIF format,
still-decode stage, exact diagnostic, and a successful retry matching a fresh
decode. The injected fault remains separate from Pillow parity and compiles
out of normal library builds.

The targeted parity and fault-contract runs passed 1/1 each. Coverage MCP's
LCOV incremental comparison found 52 newly observed lines overall, including
five in `src/codecs/avif/av1/frame.rs` at lines 3076 and 3085–3088 (0.0396
percentage points against the selected baseline). This is a limited coordinate
estimate: the local reports have no source/build receipts or test receipts.
Coverage MCP could not provide the branch-level delta because these reports do
not contain exact branch observations. No full coverage campaign was run.
Reports: `target/release-evidence/coverage-avif-monochrome-group-baseline-current.info`,
`target/release-evidence/coverage-avif-monochrome-group-fault-current.info`.
The coverage-origin inventory now records 149 exact guards across 25 Rust
files; this is a static provenance count, not a new full-coverage measurement.

### BMP RLE4 edge parity and palette-reservation fault contract — 2026-10-15

Two active Pillow parity rows cover BI_RLE4 odd-length absolute runs: one ends
at end-of-line with the omitted low nibble, and the other places the pixel
stream at an odd file offset to exercise word padding. Their input SHA-256
values are `e126b4422eb23399b411090b0a9928b7f4f46467ea6847fbd9c0da522b6a33fb`
and `39a7b1fbc8d09716958cd9ad55f72fb477e69c40d20afceabb357807d39fff03`.
Both selected public rows pass the pinned Pillow pixel parity. The BMP fixture
generator reproduces their inputs and reference provenance.

The target-only row
`fault-contract:bmp:bmp_palette_reservation_failure` reuses the first fixture.
Its coverage-only failpoint forces the palette's fallible reservation to fail
before palette entries are read. The public contract checks the BMP
`StillDecode` error `decode: unable to allocate BMP palette` and confirms that
a clean retry equals a fresh decode. The selected fault row passed 1/1; the
normal allocation path compiles without the fault hook. Coverage MCP found no
missing branch observation at `src/codecs/bmp/decode.rs:173`, but its selected
reports have no source/build receipts or test attribution, and branch-level
incremental comparison is incomparable because exact detail is incomplete.
No aggregate coverage gain or full-coverage result is claimed.
Selected reports: `target/release-evidence/coverage-bmp-rle4-odd-eol-current.json`,
`target/release-evidence/coverage-bmp-rle4-odd-offset-current.json`, and
`target/release-evidence/coverage-bmp-palette-fault-current.json`.

The public parity row `decode:jpeg:baseline_420_reversed_chroma_sos_order`

parity row using the deterministic 8×8 baseline 4:4:4 input with a valid COM

The first focused run exposed a public decode failure: the single-scan fast
boundary check rejected COM as a non-DQT marker, then generic entropy
extraction treated COM as entropy and returned no segment. The parser had
already recorded the end of scan entropy. The decoder now reuses that
boundary for a single baseline scan when parsed COM or DQT segments precede
EOI. This keeps entropy extraction bounded at the scan and avoids additional
pixel processing. The selected matrix row passes.

### JPEG entropy-boundary regression guard — 2026-10-17

GitHub CI #658 exposed two regressions in the initial COM fix on x86-64 and
Windows: a fill byte before an RST marker shortened entropy extraction, and
an unexpected `FF02` marker after entropy was accepted by the fast path. The
boundary helper now walks the post-scan tail and only accepts well-formed COM
and DQT segments. Restart markers and other marker codes fall back to generic
entropy extraction, which preserves RST splitting and malformed-marker
rejection.

The selected matrix run passed the COM parity case, the restart-marker-fill
case, and the malformed unexpected-marker case. Its LLVM report is
`target/release-evidence/coverage-jpeg-tail-regressions.json`; Coverage MCP
reports 367/31,392 branch outcomes for this selection. Its source receipt and
test attribution are absent, and comparison with the historical full report
is incomparable because the baseline detail does not reconcile with its
totals. This is selected-run evidence only; it does not establish aggregate
coverage change.

Added the active public row
`decode:tiff:compression_deflate_be_unsigned16_wraparound_predictor`. The

Predictor=2. Its rows include modulo-65,536 underflow and overflow deltas. The

big-endian delta reconstruction is required for the sample comparison to pass.

## WebP quality-80 method-4 flat-block parity — 2026-10-27

The mismatch came from libwebp's `PickBestIntra16` scoring rule: for a uniform
source macroblock, it doubles distortion and spectral distortion while the
quantized luma AC coefficients remain flat, then stops applying the rule once
a candidate is no longer flat. The Rust encoder omitted that ordered update
and could select Intra16 where Pillow/libwebp selected Intra4. The Rust path
now applies the method-3-or-higher rate-distortion rule in candidate order.

Added active Pillow rows
`encode:webp:enc_lossy_quality_80_method_4_uniform_rgb_32x32` and
`encode:webp:enc_lossy_quality_80_method_4_nonuniform_rgb_17x17`. The uniform
32x32 output is 80 bytes (SHA-256
`d5b33a6a4452d87928c7956be970a09f66bf33b024f91df67b61222017617f3d`); the
nonuniform 17x17 edge-padded output is 380 bytes (SHA-256
`9c01cd551254909ec5028d6470d2f83af7ab936fc0146c9b9738432d40f6df10`). Both
selected public parity rows passed, including exact reference bytes and
re-decode pixel parity: 2/2 rows, 8 encode calls, no failures or panics. The
selected LLVM report is
`.coverage-mcp/local-evidence/selected/webp-flat-intra16-q80-m4-final-20261027/coverage.json`
(SHA-256
`441c71287eb33384d45ac980f60ab81306037d03c68dff1672e878aabbf595ec`).
Coverage MCP still returns `I/O error: No such file or directory` for reports
inside this managed worktree, so the report is local LLVM evidence without

The current `Directory::parse` constructs each numeric entry's byte length as
`count * type_size`, where supported types have a nonzero width. After the
`count == 0` early return, division by the count therefore yields that exact
nonzero width, and the byte length is divisible by the count. The later
`chunks_exact` remainder check is consequently false for entries produced by
the public parser. These arithmetic rejection branches do not describe
reachable malformed-file behavior; no private unit tests or duplicate parity
rows were added. The active mixed-width and empty-field rows cover Pillow's
first-page output and record its sequence-enumeration failures for unusable
later-page metadata.

## AV1 integer-motion block copy — 2026-10-29

`put_unscaled_kernel` now copies complete in-bounds rows when both interpolation
filters are absent, which is the integer-motion path. The checked `PlaneView`
row slices feed `copy_from_slice`; filtered blocks and any block touching a
plane edge keep the existing replicated-sample kernel. This adds no unsafe code
or allocation. It leaves the existing `wide` SIMD kernels intact; compiler
lowering and runtime speed on x86 still need native measurement.

The public sequence probe was rebuilt with all features and measured the same
three-frame motion-range input in sequential A-B-B-A order, 51 decoder calls
per run and two runs per build. Across 102 measured calls per build, the
control median was 13.224 ms and nearest-rank p95 was 14.527 ms; the candidate median was
12.666 ms and p95 was 13.406 ms, a 4.22% lower median on this ARM64 host. The
candidate and control binary hashes, toolchain, host, and raw runs are retained
in `.coverage-mcp/local-evidence/perf/20261029-avif-motion-mv-copy-candidate/`.
This is one workload on a dirty tree, not a world-record or x86 SIMD claim.

## JPEG ZRL batching trial — 2026-10-31

A release sample of RGB 512×512 Q10 4:2:0 encoding identified repeated AC
zero-run-length (ZRL) Huffman writes in `encode_raw_ac_value`. A candidate
combined two adjacent ZRL codes into one `RawBlockWriter::write` call; each
code is at most 16 bits, so the combined call stays within the writer's
32-bit bound and emits the same bit sequence. The candidate was built with
`CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/jpeg-zrl-batch-arm64-20261031 cargo build
--manifest-path benchmarks/jpeg-production/rust/Cargo.toml --release
--locked`. Baseline and candidate binary SHA-256 values are
`ae481f7245766a33ebda4d46826a09540a3fe0820822a824590b691c4ddadd64` and
`5229207069b68731555a9d9f96f473dfbed999a6103975fa90bc4422b0686d69`.

Three A–B–B–A cohorts ran the same generated 512×512 RGB, quality-10,
4:2:0 workload for 1,200 iterations per process with 100 warmups. The input
FNV-1a was `75efb3d33c9418ec`; all twelve runs emitted 29,341 bytes with FNV-1a
`4280bc9f48852fbe`. Candidate paired medians were about 1.5%, 3.2%, and 2.6%
slower than their controls. Across all six runs per build, the medians were
1,523,813 ns baseline and 1,554,063 ns candidate. Host load averages started
at 8.44 and remained above 6.8, so these timings do not establish the exact
regression size; they provide no evidence of a gain. The candidate was
rejected and the JPEG source was restored without a retained code change.

Selected public parity passed 2/2 for `encode:jpeg:enc_q10` and
`encode:jpeg:enc_optimize`, including exact reference outputs and 128×128
re-decode pixel parity. Its local LLVM report is

`834c2de6261d4445fbe65bec3eb2f5edce478c1d1da1de3bd2c9eb730f7189ae`).

## JPEG progressive restart interval cleanup — 2026-10-31

The latest local full LLVM report showed an unobserved true outcome for
`current_restart_interval.is_some()` at `src/codecs/jpeg/encode/mod.rs:5127`
in both `Noop` and token checkpoint instantiations of
`encode_progressive_scans_exact`. Coverage MCP returned `Transport closed` for
the full report and the focused report, so this finding is local LLVM evidence,
not MCP attribution.

Source inspection established the state invariant: `restart_rows` is fixed
for one encode; every scan interval is zero when row restarts are disabled (or
the row count exceeds Pillow's limit), and positive otherwise because every
valid scan has at least one MCU column. The current interval can change between
positive scan intervals, but cannot transition from nonzero to zero. The
redundant `current_restart_interval.is_some()` fallback was removed, leaving
the direct `restart_interval != 0` marker condition.

Selected Pillow parity passed 4/4 for `encode:jpeg:enc_progressive`,
`encode:jpeg:enc_progressive_restart_rows`,
`encode:jpeg:enc_progressive_restart_rows_partial_mcu_420`, and
`encode:jpeg:enc_cmyk_progressive_restart_rows`. The LLVM report is

## JPEG MCU offset arithmetic trial — 2026-10-31

A targeted experiment replaced saturating arithmetic for MCU-derived offsets
inside `encode_baseline_420_mcu_row_streaming` with ordinary addition and
multiplication. Allocation sizing and restart countdown saturation were left
unchanged. Release binaries on Apple M3 Pro with Rust 1.96.1 ran the public
512×512 RGB Q10 4:2:0 encode with the same deterministic input (FNV-1a
`75efb3d33c9418ec`), 100 warmup calls, and 1,000 measured calls per process.
Two A–B–B–A sequences produced these per-process medians:

| Sequence | Baseline A (ms) | Candidate B (ms) | Candidate B (ms) | Baseline A (ms) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 1.462709 | 1.499000 | 1.481000 | 1.450667 |
| 2 | 1.464709 | 1.437875 | 1.454417 | 1.454542 |

The median of the four baseline process medians was 1.458626 ms; the candidate
was 1.467709 ms, 0.62% slower. The direction reversed between sequences, so
there was no stable speedup. Every run produced 29,341 bytes with FNV-1a
`4280bc9f48852fbe`, matching the retained TurboJPEG comparison for this input.
The candidate was rejected and the source restored. This targeted ARM64
diagnostic does not establish SSE2 or AVX2 runtime performance.

## WebP VP8 method-one lossy encoder parity — 2026-10-31

Added active parity row `encode:webp:enc_lossy_method_1_intra16_candidate_pruning`
for the existing 128×128 RGB WebP source at quality 80, method 1. The first run
exposed a mismatch: Rust produced 4,056 bytes while Pillow produced 4,088.

pixel distortion and fixed mode cost before quantization. The Rust encoder now

## WebP VP8 segment-map update parity — 2026-10-31
